claim_formal: ∀ q, ∀ Dirichlet character χ mod q, ∀ s ∈ ℂ with Re s > 7/8, (χ,s) ≠ (1,1): L(s,χ) ≠ 0 (in particular ζ(s) ≠ 0)

quote_A.text: Every finite-order Hecke $L$-function over $F=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ has no zero in $\Re s>7/8$. The same holds for every Dirichlet $L$-function, including $\zeta(s)$.

quote_B.text: Theorem~\ref{thm:main} resolves the quasi-Riemann hypothesis affirmatively

notes: Zero-free half-plane read as non-existence of zeros (M4); M1 also defensible. Lean covers ζ and Dirichlet L (same); Hecke over Q(√-3) only partially in Lean. Companions: alternate 11/12 proof, uniform exclusion of Landau–Siegel zeros ((1-β)log q ≥ c). Corollaries: Vinogradov least nonresidue conjecture, deterministic square roots, idoneal numbers.

claim_formal: ∀ prime n ≥ 5, ∀ sequences (K_i,M_i,σ_i) of totally real degree-n fields with full lattices and D(M_i) → ∞: μ_{K_i,M_i,σ_i} → m_n weakly (Haar, no escape of mass)

quote_A.text: For every fixed prime $n\ge5$ and every sequence $(K_i,M_i,\sigma_i)$ as above with \mbox{$D(M_i)\to\infty$}, \[ \mu_{K_i,M_i,\sigma_i}\longrightarrow m_n. \]

quote_B.text: We prove the packet form of the higher-dimensional Duke equidistribution problem for totally real fields of any fixed prime degree at least five

notes: Equidistribution (weak convergence) labelled M1 property. The higher-dimensional Duke problem is posed for all degrees; this family covers prime degree ≥5, primitive quartic, and primitive sextic, so O5/restricted_range (composite degrees remain). Lean is the prime-degree statement.

claim_formal: ∀ smooth connected complex curve X, ∀ r ≥ 1, ∀ quasi-unipotent classes C_1..C_s: ∃ finite extension L/K such that M_r(X)(O_L) ∩ Y(ℂ) is Zariski dense in Y (every component)

quote_A.text: There is a finite extension $L/K$ such that \[ M_r(X)(\cO_L)\cap Y(\C) \] is Zariski dense in $Y$, and hence in every irreducible component of $Y$.

quote_B.text: Resolves the determinant-one curve case of Litt's integral-density question.

notes: Litt's question is posed for character varieties of smooth (projective/quasi-projective) varieties; curve SL_r case only → O5. Litt's survey question (Question 5.4.3) treated as P2 (not a numbered problem database); P3 arguable. Lean comparator is an intermediate seam-equation lemma (different). M2 vs M1 (density is a property of the integral points) borderline.

claim_formal: ∀ r ≥ 10, ∀ᵍ (p_1..p_r) ∈ U_r (very general), ∀ nonzero effective plane curve C of degree d, ∀ m_i ≤ mult_{p_i} C: Σ m_i < d√r

quote_A.text: If $C$ is a nonzero effective plane curve of degree $d\ge1$ and $m_1,\ldots,m_r\in\Z_{\ge0}$ satisfy $\mult_{p_i}C\ge m_i$, then \[ d\sqrt r>\sum_{i=1}^r m_i. \]

quote_B.text: establishes Nagata's conjecture in its strict, nonhomogeneous form

notes: Nagata's inequality read as a one-sided bound (M8); M1 (inequality between given objects) defensible, and it implies the exact Seshadri constant 1/√r (M9 reading). Other manuscripts: qualitative Nagata–Biran–Szemberg for surfaces, higher dimensions and positive characteristic (eventual maximal Seshadri constants, ∀ X ∀^∞ r ∀ᵍ p, M9).

claim_formal: ∀ compact connected Kähler X (dim ≥ 2), ∀ splitting T_X = E_1 ⊕ E_2 into integrable holomorphic subbundles of positive rank: ∃ simply connected Y_1,Y_2 and biholomorphism Φ: X̃ → Y_1 × Y_2 with dΦ(π*E_i) = pr_i*T_{Y_i}

quote_A.text: there are connected simply connected complex manifolds $Y_1,Y_2$ and a biholomorphism $\Phi:\widetilde X\to Y_1\times Y_2$ such that \[ \dd\Phi(\pi^*E_i)=\pr_i^*T_{Y_i}\qquad(i=1,2), \]

quote_B.text: We prove the two-summand form of Beauville's compatible splitting conjecture.

notes: Beauville's conjecture is posed for any number of summands; two-summand case → O5. Companion: integrability of split tangent bundles on rationally connected manifolds proves Höring's conjecture (P1/O1, ∀ M1). Both have Lean comparators.

claim_formal: ∀ smooth complete intersection X ⊂ ℙ^N_ℂ: the ordinary unreduced total descendant potential Z_X satisfies L_k Z_X = 0 for all k ≥ −1 (all genera, curve classes, insertions)

quote_A.text: Let \(X\subset\PP^N_\C\) be a smooth complete intersection. Its ordinary, unreduced total descendant potential satisfies the Virasoro constraints in every genus and curve class

quote_B.text: We prove the Virasoro conjecture for the ordinary descendant Gromov–Witten theory of smooth complete intersections in projective space

notes: Virasoro conjecture is posed for all smooth projective varieties; this settles the class of complete intersections (O5). Companion: Virasoro constraints pass to projectivizations of vector bundles (V(B) ⇒ V(P(E)), M1, O8-like).

claim_formal: ∀ δ > 0: T_δ is bounded on L^3(ℝ^3) (hence ∀ 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞ with δ > max{3|1/p−1/2|−1/2,0}: T_δ bounded on L^p(ℝ^3))

quote_A.text: For every $\delta>0$, there is a finite constant $C_\delta$ such that \begin{equation} \norm{T_\delta f}_{L^3(\RR^3)} \le C_\delta\norm f_{L^3(\RR^3)}

quote_B.text: We prove the three-dimensional Bochner–Riesz conjecture in its strict-order formulation.

notes: Bochner–Riesz conjecture is posed in all dimensions; settling n=3 → O5 per rule 6 (O1 if the 3D case is counted as its own problem). Boundedness with an unspecified constant labelled M1 (M8 possible); constants not explicit.

claim_formal: ∀ smooth nonnegative completely monotone g on (0,∞), ∀ locally finite C ⊂ ℝ² of centered disk density one: E_g(C) ≥ Σ_{a∈A∖0} g(|a|²) = E_g(A) (triangular lattice A attains the minimum)

quote_A.text: For every smooth nonnegative completely monotone function $g$ on $(0,\infty)$ and every locally finite planar set $\mathcal C$ of centered disk density one, \[ E_g(\mathcal C)\ge \sum_{a\in A\setminus\{0\}}g(|a|^2)=E_g(A). \]

quote_B.text: We prove universal energy minimality for the triangular lattice in the plane.

notes: Optimality with attainment by the triangular lattice → M9 (M1 defensible). Problem taken as the planar universal-optimality conjecture (Cohn–Kumar), not named in the excerpt, hence moderate B confidence. Other results: Sandier–Serfaty conjecture (Coulomb renormalized energy minimized by triangular lattice), 2D Brauchart–Hardin–Saff linear term, planar Cohn–Elkies sharpness conjecture (∃ certificate f, M2), sharp Gaussian minorants.

claim_formal: ∀ ε,δ ∈ (0,1/2): ∃ s ≥ 1 and a deterministic poly-time reduction 3SAT → explicit unweighted Unique Games over F_2^s with completeness ≥ 1−ε and soundness ≤ δ (UG is NP-hard)

quote_A.text: For every fixed \(\varepsilon,\delta\in(0,1/2)\), there are an integer \(s\ge1\) and a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from \(\mathrm{3SAT}\) to explicit unweighted Unique Games instances

quote_B.text: We prove the Unique Games Conjecture.

notes: Companions give direct NP-hardness proofs: Max-Cut beyond Goemans–Williamson, Vertex Cover below 2, Min-UnCut and DFVS within any constant (all M10).

claim_formal: ∃ uniform randomized algorithm ∀ pair of integral polymatroids (rank-value oracles, equal total rank, binary capacities) ∀ ε,δ: outputs Ẑ with P((1−ε)Z ≤ Ẑ ≤ (1+ε)Z) ≥ 1−δ using poly(n, ℓ, 1/ε, log 1/δ) oracle calls and bit operations on every run

quote_A.text: There is a single uniform randomized algorithm which, for every input described above, outputs a nonnegative rational $\widehat Z$ satisfying \[ \PP\bigl((1-\eps)Z\le\widehat Z\le(1+\eps)Z\bigr) \ge1-\delta. \]

quote_B.text: Gives a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for counting common integer bases of two integral polymatroids of equal total rank

notes: Posed question (from matroid companion .tex): FPRAS for common bases of two independence-oracle matroids, Liu's dissertation Section 13.2 Problem 1 (P2; arguably P3 as a numbered problem). Headline polymatroid result settles it in a more general form; O8 also defensible. Lean comparator is the two-matroid FPRAS, a special case of the polymatroid headline (weaker).

claim_formal: ∀ n ≥ 1, ∀ 1 ≤ d ≤ n, ∀ real multilinear p of degree ≤ d: f = sgn(p) satisfies I(f) ≤ 8d√n

quote_A.text: Let $n\ge1$ and $1\le d\le n$ be integers. Let $p$ be a real multilinear polynomial of degree at most $d$ ... Then, for average sensitivity under the uniform law, \[ I(f)\le 8d\sqrt n. \]

quote_B.text: This proves the asymptotic form of the Gotsman–Linial conjecture.

notes: The exact Gotsman–Linial extremal form was already refuted (Chapman, Kim–Maldonado–Wellens); the asymptotic O(d√n) form is the conjecture settled.

claim_formal: γ* = 0: ∀ ε > 0 ∃ C_ε ∀ d ≥ 2: Q(d) ≤ C_ε d^ε, and ∃ c, d_0 ∀ d ≥ d_0: Q(d) ≥ c log d (Q = first-order query complexity of sampling well-conditioned log-concave laws to TV 1/10)

quote_A.text: In the oracle model above, for every \(\varepsilon>0\) there is \(C_\varepsilon<\infty\) such that \[ Q(d)\le C_\varepsilon d^\varepsilon \qquad(d\ge2). \] ... In particular, \(\gamma_*=0\).

quote_B.text: is a positive power of the dimension intrinsically necessary, or is it a feature of the sampling algorithms used? We answer this question in the exact first-order oracle model ... The optimal dimension exponent is zero.

notes: Read as determining an exponent exactly (rule 7: P4/O1/M9). Alternative: P2 question 'is a positive power necessary?' answered no (O2), or the upper bound alone as M8 with prefix ∀∃. Prefix 'none' treats γ* as a pre-existing named exponent; ∀∃∀ if read off the upper-bound formula.

claim_formal: ∃ q ≥ 1, ∃ C¹ self-map f of M = (ℝ/100ℤ) × (S²)^{q+1}: h_top(f) = 0 ∧ f_* on H_2(M;ℝ) has eigenvalue 2 (so h_top(f) < log ρ(f_*))

quote_A.text: There are a positive integer \(q\) and a \(C^1\) self-map \(f\) of the compact smooth manifold ... such that \(\htop(f)=0\) and \(f_*:H_2(M;\R)\to H_2(M;\R)\) has eigenvalue \(2\).

quote_B.text: We disprove the general C1 self-map formulation of Shub's entropy conjecture.

notes: Refutes the general C¹ self-map (noninvertible) formulation (Saghin–Xia Conjecture 1); the diffeomorphism formulation is untouched. No corrected statement offered, so O2 not O3.

claim_formal: ∀ r, m ≥ 1, ∀ colouring χ: ℕ → [r]: ∃ distinct a_1 < … < a_m and colour c with χ(Σ_{j∈J} a_j) = χ(Π_{j∈J} a_j) = c for every nonempty J ⊆ [m]

quote_A.text: For every coloring $\chi:\N\to[r]$, there are distinct positive integers $a_1<\cdots<a_m$ and a color $c\in[r]$ such that

quote_B.text: We prove Hindman's finite sums and products conjecture

notes: Also recorded as Hindman–Strauss Question 17.18 (a book question, not a problem database).

claim_formal: ∀ n ≥ 2, ∀ finite simple graph H with h = e(H) ≥ 1 edges and ≤ n vertices: p_c(n,H) ≤ min{1, 2048e^50 p_E(n,H)(1+log_2 h)}

quote_B.text: We prove the second Kahn–Kalai conjecture.

notes: Deterministic inequality between thresholds of G(n,p); probabilistic flag because the objects are random-graph thresholds.

claim_formal: For the uniform triangle-removal process on K_n: E[(F_n/n^{3/2} − 1/(2√2))²] → 0 (hence F_n/n^{3/2} → 1/(2√2) in probability and in mean)

quote_A.text: For the uniform triangle-removal process starting from $K_n$, \[ \E\left[\left(\frac{F_n}{n^{3/2}}- \frac1{2\sqrt2}\right)^2\right]\longrightarrow0. \]

quote_B.text: This proves the triangle case of the sharp-constant conjecture of Joos and Kühn.

notes: Joos–Kühn Conjecture 16.2 covers general strictly balanced hypergraph removal; the triangle case only → O5 per rule 6. Also confirms the Bollobás–Erdős n^{3/2} order with sharp constant.

claim_formal: ∀ n ≥ 1, ∀ 2 ≤ a_1 ≤ … ≤ a_n, ∀ homogeneous I ⊆ ℂ[x_1..x_n] containing a regular sequence of degrees a_i: the lex-plus-powers J exists, is an ideal with the same Hilbert function, and β_{p,j}(S/I) ≤ β_{p,j}(S/J) ∀ p,j (extended to every char-0 field and any length c)

quote_A.text: the spaces in \eqref{eq:prescription} exist and \(J=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}J_d\) is a homogeneous ideal. For this single ideal, \[ \beta^S_{p,j}(S/I)\le\beta^S_{p,j}(S/J) \qquad\text{for every \(p\ge0\) and \(j\in\Z\)}. \]

quote_B.text: We prove the Eisenbud–Green–Harris and lex-plus-powers conjectures over every characteristic-zero field

notes: EGH and LPP are usually stated over an arbitrary field; only characteristic zero is proved, so O5/restricted_range (O1 if char 0 is taken as the intended setting). Matrix borderline: existence of the extremal ideal (M2) vs Betti inequality between I and its prescribed J (M1). The Artinian-over-ℂ case uses established Artinian reductions (Caviglia–Maclagan, Caviglia–Kummini) to reach the full char-0 statement.

claim_formal: ∀ nonatomic law G on [0,∞) with E[min(X_1..X_4)²] < ∞: almost surely there is no bigeodesic in planar FPP with iid G weights

quote_A.text: Then, with probability one, there is no sequence \((v_i)_{i\in\Z}\) of pairwise distinct vertices with consecutive vertices adjacent and

quote_B.text: This resolves the planar no-bigeodesics conjecture under that moment assumption.

notes: The conjecture is for iid continuous laws; proved under a minimum-of-four second-moment assumption (O5, restricted class of laws). Companion: exponential limit shape strictly convex and C¹; Gamma-law differentiability. Both Lean comparators formalize the limit-shape results, not the headline (different).

claim_formal: ∀ bounded Jordan domain D, ∀ distinct counterclockwise marks a,b,c,d: lim_{ε→0} P(C_ε(D;a,b,c,d)) = F(x) (Cardy's formula, annealed, critical Poisson–Voronoi percolation)

quote_A.text: For every bounded Jordan domain $D$ and every four distinct counterclockwise boundary marks $a,b,c,d$, one has \begin{equation}\label{eq:cardy} \lim_{\eps\downarrow0}\PP\bigl(\mathcal C_\eps(D;a,b,c,d)\bigr) =F(x)

quote_B.text: The theorem resolves positively the annealed Cardy-crossing conjecture for critical Poisson--Voronoi percolation, the crossing-probability aspect of Schramm's Problem~2.12

notes: Schramm's Problem 2.12 (numbered problem collection, P3) asks for full conformal invariance for Voronoi percolation; only the annealed crossing-probability aspect is proved → O5. Prefix: limit of (deterministic) crossing probabilities, so ∀ rather than ℙ; rule 4 could argue for ∀ℙ. Companions (conditional on Cardy for Voronoi): pivotal amplitude ε^{3/4} asymptotics and quenched near-critical universality.

claim_formal: ∀ d ≥ 3, ∀ β ≥ 0: μ_{d,β} (free zero-field Ising on T_d) is a factor of IID ⇔ tanh β ≤ (d−1)^{−1/2}

quote_A.text: For every integer $d\ge3$ and every $\beta\ge0$, the free zero-field Ising law $\mu_{d,\beta}$ is a factor of IID in the sense of \eqref{eq:equivariance} if and only if \[ \tanh\beta\le(d-1)^{-1/2}. \]

quote_B.text: We prove the positive implication, including equality, resolving the conjecture of Nam, Sly and Zhang; the strict converse is known.

notes: Exact threshold read as M9; M5 (iff characterization) equally defensible. The new content is the positive direction (∃ factor map); the converse is due to Sly/Lyons, hence full_only_with_prior_results. Also the ferromagnetic case of Lyons's question.

claim_formal: Thompson's group F is not amenable

quote_A.text: Thompson's group \(F\) is not amenable.

quote_B.text: This confirms Geoghegan's conjecture and resolves the amenability problem for F.

notes: Read as Geoghegan's nonamenability conjecture confirmed (O1). Read as the amenability question 'is F amenable?' it would be P2/O2.

claim_formal: ∀ n ≥ 3, ∀ smooth one-ended initial-data exterior (Ω^n,g,K) with DEC, weakly future-trapped boundary, stated decay, E > |P|, A_min(S) > 0: m ≥ ½ (A_min(S)/ω_{n−1})^{(n−2)/(n−1)} (sharp)

quote_A.text: Then \begin{equation}\label{eq:setting:main} m\geq\frac12\left(\frac{A_{\min,g}(S)}{\omega_{n-1}} \right)^{\frac{n-2}{n-1}}. \end{equation} The coefficient and exponent are sharp in each dimension $n\geq3$.

quote_B.text: We prove the sharp spacetime Penrose inequality for smooth one-ended initial-data exteriors in every spatial dimension n ≥ 3

notes: Sharp inequality attained by Schwarzschild (M9; M8 defensible). The enclosing-area formulation with decay hypotheses could be read as a restricted form of the spacetime Penrose conjecture (O5). Family is large: charged/dyonic version, higher-dimensional electric reduction, Kerr–Newman axisymmetric version plus counterexamples with electromagnetic tails, AdS/asymptotically hyperbolic versions, rigidity. Lean comparator is the CKS end-replacement lemma (different).

claim_formal: ∃ explicit entangled density operator ρ on ℂ^10 ⊗ ℂ^10 (range has no product vector) with K_D(ρ) = 0 for all admitted completed protocols

quote_A.text: There is an explicitly specified entangled density operator $\rho$ on $\C^{10}\otimes\C^{10}$ whose range contains no nonzero product vector and for which $K_D(\rho)=0$.

quote_B.text: A trace-preserving PPT channel on $`M_{21}(\mathbb C)`$ whose square is not entanglement breaking disproves Christandl's PPT-square conjecture.

notes: From the intro .tex: the posed question is Problem 24 'Secret key from all entangled states' in Krüger–Werner's open-problem collection (P3), answered negatively by an example (M3, rule 5). Second headline: the PPT² conjecture refuted (P1/O2, ∃ M3), and the two-map PPT-composition conjecture (Christandl–Müller-Hermes–Wolf) refuted. The quote_B is from the PPT² part. The key result holds for the paper's specified protocol class. Lean formalizes the PPT pair and the M_21 channel, not the key state (different).

claim_formal: α_tot = 4: R(f) = O((1+Q(f))^4) for all total Boolean f, and ∀ k ≥ 2 ∃ total F_{k,m} with Q ≤ C_k √m (log m)^{b_k} and R ≥ c_k m^{2−1/k}/(log m)^2

quote_A.text: The optimal power is $\alpha_{\mathrm{tot}}=4$.

quote_B.text: Thus the known quartic upper bound has the optimal exponent, disproving the conjectured cubic bound.

notes: Rule 7: refutes the conjectured cubic value and determines the true exponent → O3. The upper bound R = O(Q^4) was already known, and the new content is the separating family (∀k ∃F, which is M3 against the cubic conjecture). Could also be read as P4/O1.

claim_formal: ∀ type II_1 factor M with separable predual: ∃ x ∈ M with M = W*(x) (equivalently two self-adjoint generators)

quote_A.text: Every type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $M$ with separable predual is generated by two self-adjoint elements. Equivalently, there is an $x\in M$ such that $M=W^*(x)$.

quote_B.text: Combined with the established direct-integral reduction to this case, this gives an affirmative solution of the generator problem for von Neumann algebras with separable predual.

notes: The generator problem (all separable-predual vN algebras) follows via Willig's direct-integral reduction (prior result). It is often counted among Kadison's problems, but no numbered list is cited in the excerpt, so P2. Stronger result: relative generation (unitaries generating M over an irreducible P form a dense G_δ, ∀ᵍ-type).

claim_formal: ∀ n ≥ 0: ∃ prime p ∃ finite p-local spectrum X with BP_*X ≅ BP_*/(p,v_1,…,v_n) as BP_*BP-comodules

quote_A.text: For every integer $n\geq0$, there exist a prime $p$ and a finite $p$-local spectrum $X$ such that \[ \BP_*X\cong\BP_*/(p,v_1,\ldots,v_n) \]

quote_B.text: Thus the all-height Smith--Toda existence problem has a positive answer when the prime may depend on the height.

notes: The Smith–Toda realization problem is usually posed at a fixed prime (for which p does V(n) exist?). Here the prime may vary with n and there is no bound on p, so it is read as a weakened form (O5); O1 for the varying-prime formulation is also plausible. Companion: explicit V(4) at p = 1009 (∃, specific instance).

claim_formal: ∃ closed connected aspherical topological 4-manifolds M, N: M ≃ N (homotopy equivalent) ∧ M ≇ N (not homeomorphic), with common word-hyperbolic π_1

quote_A.text: There exist closed connected aspherical topological four-manifolds $M$ and $N$ that are homotopy equivalent but not homeomorphic.

quote_B.text: disproving the homeomorphism-existence formulation of the Borel conjecture in dimension four

notes: Counterexample in dimension 4 refutes the Borel conjecture as a universal statement (O2). If the dimension-four case is counted as its own problem, still O2. Also: a self-homotopy equivalence not homotopic to a homeomorphism.

claim_formal: N_2(ℓ_1) ≤ 12√21 < ∞ (real ℓ_1 has metric Markov cotype two)

quote_A.text: The real space $\ell_1$ satisfies \[ N_2(\ell_1)\leq12\sqrt{21}. \]

quote_B.text: We prove that the real Banach space ℓ1 has metric Markov cotype two, answering a question of Mendel and Naor.

notes: Explicit bound with finiteness as the qualitative content (M8; M1 'ℓ1 has the property' also possible). Corollary: Ball's Lipschitz extension problem for Hilbert space to ℓ1 targets.

claim_formal: ∀ connected closed smooth Riemannian (M,g) of positive dimension: inj(M,g) = diam(M,g) → (M,g) is, up to scaling, a round sphere, ℝP^n, ℂP^n, ℍP^n or the Cayley plane

quote_A.text: If $\inj(M,g)=\diam(M,g)$, then $(M,g)$ is isometric, up to multiplication of the metric by a positive constant, to a round sphere, a standard real, complex or quaternionic projective space, or the Cayley plane.

quote_B.text: We prove the metric Blaschke conjecture

notes: Classification of Blaschke manifolds (M6); M5 also possible, since the converse (CROSSes are Blaschke) is classical. Also a sharp volume comparison Vol(M) ≥ Vol(M_0) with rigidity.

claim_formal: ∀ n ≥ 2, ∀ κ ∈ ℝ, ∀ complete separable metric space (M,d): (M,d) is n-dim Alexandrov with curv ≥ κ ⇔ (M,d,H^n) is full-support RCD((n−1)κ,n) with distributional sectional curvature ≥ κ

quote_A.text: The following conditions are equivalent. ... \((M,d)\) is an \(n\)-dimensional Alexandrov space with curvature bounded below by \(\kappa\). ... \((M,d,m)\) has full support, is \(\RCD((n-1)\kappa,n)\)

quote_B.text: This resolves Gigli's characterization conjecture in dimensions at least two.

notes: 'In dimensions at least two' may signal that n = 1 is excluded (O5 possible). The Lean comparator is the weak-Hessian-along-geodesics lemma from the companion paper (different).

claim_formal: ∀ bounded domains Ω, Λ ⊂ ℝ³, ∀ 1 ≤ p < ∞, ∀ homeomorphism f ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω;ℝ³) onto Λ: ∃ C^∞ diffeomorphisms f_j: Ω → Λ with f_j → f strongly in W^{1,p}

quote_A.text: There exist $C^\infty$ diffeomorphisms $f_j:\Omega\to\Lambda$, each belonging to $W^{1,p}(\Omega;\R^3)$, such that

quote_B.text: Resolves the three-dimensional Ball–Evans approximation problem

notes: The Ball–Evans question is posed in general dimension (planar case known), so settling n = 3 is O5 per rule 6; O1 if the 3D problem is counted as its own. Split across two manuscripts: 1 ≤ p ≤ 2 and p > 2.
